chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

Whoever sets right his inward self, Allah sets right his outward self, and whoever works for his religion, Allah suffices him with the affairs of his world, and whoever is good in what is between him and Allah, Allah makes good what is between him and the people.

key_terms.سَرِيرَتَهُ: his inward self or inner state
key_terms.عَلاَنِيَتَهُ: his outward self or public affairs

ai.seo_question: How does inner sincerity affect outward success in Islam?
ai.summary: In the context of Nahj al-Balagha, this hadith articulates the principle of *mu'atabah* (divine correspondence), where the internal state of the heart dictates external reality. Shia scholars emphasize that 'rectifying the *sarirah*' involves aligning one's hidden intentions with divine will, thereby ensuring that Allah manages worldly affairs as a consequence of spiritual fidelity rather than mere effort.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 423. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

Whoever set right his inward self, Allāh sets right his outward self. Whoever performs acts for his religion, Allāh accomplishes his acts of this world. Whoever’s dealings between himself and Allāh are good, Allāh turns the dealings between him and other people good.
